name: Chen Baozhen
current_role: Co-founder and major (5%+) shareholder of Wangsu Science & Technology (ChinaNetCenter), Shenzhen-listed 300017; not an executive
profile: Chen Baozhen co-founded the predecessor of Wangsu Science & Technology, a Shanghai CDN/edge-computing and internet infrastructure provider, in 2000 after ~30 years at a Fujian electrical-instrument factory. She sold much of her stake in 2018-2020 and further reductions were announced in 2024; she remains a 5%+ holder.
interesting_fact: She started her career in 1960 at an electrical instrument factory in Fujian and stayed 30 years before co-founding what became one of China's largest CDN / data-center service companies at around age 60.

public_contacts.value: Wangsu investor Q&A via Shenzhen Stock Exchange Hudongyi platform (stock code 300017) / p5w IR platform

notes: Very private; no interviews found. Wangsu (CDN/edge/data centers) is highly relevant to a data-center podcast, but the operational leaders are chairman Li Boyang and board secretary Zhou Liping; route any request via Wangsu's board office. Search usage limits limited depth.

name: Meyer "Micky" Malka
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner, Ribbit Capital (Palo Alto); director of Robinhood Markets
profile: Venezuelan-born fintech investor who started and sold companies in Venezuela, co-founded Brazil's Banco Lemon (sold to Banco do Brasil) and mobile-payments firm Bling Nation/Lemon (sold to LifeLock, 2013), then founded Ribbit Capital in 2012. Ribbit was an early backer of Robinhood, Coinbase, Credit Karma and Nubank; Malka sits on Robinhood's board and Ribbit is a 10%+ holder of Root Inc.
interesting_fact: Ribbit's name comes from the sound a frog makes, meant to evoke 'leapfrogging' incumbent financial institutions.
deep_cut_fact: Before Silicon Valley he co-founded Heptagon Group, a brokerage serving Venezuelan and U.S. markets, and co-developed Patagon.com, later acquired by Banco Santander; he also co-founded Banco Bracce, a Brazilian lender to mid-sized companies.
notes: Holds an economics degree from Universidad Catolica Andres Bello (Caracas). Has appeared on the Founders podcast (David Senra) — a good sign he does long-form audio. Ribbit site lists no public email; best route likely via Ribbit or Robinhood corporate communications.

name: Li Denghai
current_role: Founder and Honorary Chairman, Shandong Denghai Seeds (SZSE 002041); chairman since 2025 is Tang Shiwei
profile: Li Denghai, a farmer's son from Laizhou, Shandong, is known as the 'father of compact hybrid corn' in China. He founded Houdeng Agricultural Experiment Station in 1985 (China's first private corn-seed enterprise), which became Denghai Seeds, listed in Shenzhen in 2005. In his late 70s he remains active as founder/honorary chairman.
interesting_fact: He set China's summer-corn yield record seven times and the world record twice, including 1,402.86 kg per mu with 'Denghai Chaoshi No.1' in 2005; his compact hybrids once covered ~43% of China's corn acreage. He and Yuan Longping are dubbed 'Southern Yuan, Northern Li'.
deep_cut_fact: After junior high in 1966 he went back to farm in Houdeng Village; at 23 (1972) he became head of the village agricultural-science team, and from 1978 spent winters breeding in Sanya, Hainan to squeeze two generations a year out of his corn lines.
notes: Emails are the company's board-office (dmb) and general mailbox as listed in the 2025 annual report. Attended the Feb 2025 private-enterprise symposium in Beijing. Agriculture rather than energy/data centers; likely Chinese-language interview only.

name: Yuan Jinyu
current_role: Chairman (since Sept 2000), Shenzhen Sunlord Electronics Co. (SZSE 002138)
profile: Yuan Jinyu (b. 1956) has chaired Sunlord Electronics since its founding in 2000; it listed in Shenzhen in 2007 and is a leading Chinese maker of chip inductors, magnetic components, RF/microwave parts and sensors. Sunlord is now pushing into data-center and AI-server power components (vertical-power inductors, tantalum capacitors) and automotive electronics.
interesting_fact: Sunlord's 2025 annual report names data centers/AI servers as a key growth driver: its magnetic components and tantalum capacitors go into GPU boards, ASICs and AI-server power modules, and it also cites fuel-cell/energy-storage applications for data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Before electronics he spent a decade (1982-1992) as manager of a supply-and-marketing company under Shenzhen Automobile Industry Corp., then ran Shenzhen Sanjiu (999) Electromechanical Equipment Co. from 1993 to 2004.
notes: Strong fit for a data-center angle (AI-server power magnetics). Low public profile; president Shi Hongyang is the operating face of the company. Email is the board-office/investor mailbox in the annual report.
